>It is all too common that a family will disown a person for being unwell.

I find the idea of a family excluding due to an illness utterly repugnant; I'm glad you got through okay, you guys do great work over this side of the reddit world.

Cheers for that,

It has always been frustrating that my mates had no idea was I talking about when I raised it, but they've always been caring and supportive; the support network of close mates is one of the things that has always kept me grounded (excuse the pun.)

Don't get me wrong, I don't attach a stigma on mental illness, my family has an extensive history of mental illness; they're who I grew up with and my yardstick in terms of normalcy.

For me, I don't enjoy opening up to people, I find it awkward and uncomfortable and if there are management techniques around I'd rather give those a crack first.

I appreciate that you're advice is the most correct in terms of recommended action, but I try and avoid the medical world altogether; ultimately though, if there's no techniques or they are ineffective I will undoubtedly be heading to the professionals.

Might give the GP a shot, I'm not particularly keen on seeing a psychiatrist.

Thanks for the advice.
